claim_summary: The work adds a structured sensor-metric and class-profile pipeline with a prompted LLM procedure that explains, validates, and names oil-well anomaly outputs.

claim_evidence.quote: can serve as an effective explainability and validation companion to an established Open-World Learning pipeline for oil well anomaly detection. The agent achieves 89.7% novelty detection with physically-grounded naming, 91% precision in validating upstream classifications, and generates sensor-specific justifications

modules.name: Baseline-event sensor metric computation
modules.scope_reason: The module transforms baseline and event windows into numerical and categorical sensor features. R3_1_TSK is no because the same window-based feature operation does not embed an anomaly output objective; counterfactually changing task objectives does not require redesigning the temporal transformation. R3_2_GTS is yes because it explicitly depends on baseline/event windows and computes temporal statistics.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - temporal feature computation is not bound to an output objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - uses baseline and event windows and computes temporal features

evidence.quote: A critical design decision is that the LLM receives structured numerical metrics, not raw time series. For each event segment, a shared metrics module computes per-sensor and cross-sensor features from the preprocessed data

modules.name: Data-driven anomaly class profiles
modules.scope_reason: The profiles organize temporal sensor statistics and domain knowledge around nine anomaly classes. R3_1_TSK is yes because the profile schema embeds anomaly-class diagnostic criteria; changing task family would require redesigning the profiles. GTS is not selected because the module's controlling scope is the anomaly diagnosis objective rather than a task-agnostic temporal service.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - class-specific anomaly profiles embed the diagnosis objective

evidence.quote: For each of the nine known anomaly classes, a knowledge profile is built by aggregating per-sensor metrics across all available training segments.
Each profile additionally includes: • Macro behavior per sensor: change type, noise level, consistency across files, dominant pattern.

modules.name: Prompted anomaly explanation and validation procedure
modules.scope_reason: The procedure requests ranked anomaly candidates, sensor-grounded explanations, validity judgments, and novelty names. R3_1_TSK is yes because these output and validation criteria are explicitly bound to anomaly diagnosis; changing task family requires changing the prompt and output schema. GTS is not selected because temporal order is input evidence, not the procedure's controlling objective.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - ranked diagnosis, validation, and novelty naming are task objectives

evidence.quote: Input: For each segment, the single-segment metrics (Section 3.2) alongside all visible class profiles (Section 3.3).
The agent receives observed metrics, known class profiles with per-sensor statistics and distinguishing features, and task-specific instructions requesting ranked JSON output with justifications.
Output: JSON with top-3 ranked candidates, per-candidate justification citing sensor evidence, confidence label (High/Medium/Low), and for novelty cases a novel_name plus novel_description.

notes: The upstream OWL detector/classifier is inherited from cited prior work and is not counted as a contribution. The source describes a fixed prompt-driven workflow; it does not say returned outputs alter subsequent actions.
